title: Finite-level pro-etale proper base change
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring with identity, let $f$ be proper, and let
$K\in\Dplus(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ carry an etale-origin witness
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] $(L,\alpha)$. Then the pro-etale exchange
map

$$
 g^{-1}Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'_*g'^{-1}K
$$

is an isomorphism. It is independent of replacing the witness by an
isomorphic witness.

note:
*Source note:* for proper base change on the pro-etale site, see Stacks
Project, Pro-etale Cohomology, Section 61.30
([Tag 09C8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C8)).

proof.text: Fix the cartesian square and compatible ringed pro-étale exchange datum of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange], with $f$ proper as understood via [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Under the chosen identifications of the coefficient sheaves on the four corners, the module pullback $Lu^*$ in [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] is canonically the exact sheaf inverse image $u^{-1}$ (the tensor factor is along an isomorphism of coefficient rings); hence its derived pullback is represented by $u^{-1}$ and the ambient map has the displayed form. Because $\Lambda$ is finite, the witness object $L\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ has torsion cohomology. Thus [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] makes the étale exchange map for $L$ an isomorphism. The fully faithful comparison [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] transports this isomorphism to the pro-étale site, and [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] identifies the transported map with the pro-étale exchange transformation of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for $\nu_X^*L$. The witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] supplies $\alpha:\nu_X^*L\simeq K$, so conjugating by $\alpha$ gives the displayed exchange map for $K$ and proves it is an isomorphism. If the witness is replaced by an isomorphic witness, naturality of the transported exchange transformation makes the two resulting maps conjugate by that isomorphism, hence equal as the witness-independent map.
